style: Say evenly and warmly, like a calm college writing professor reading over your shoulder.
lines: Tap a card that sparks something. Then type a small moment in the box and tap Add spark.
Tick both checks if it happened in one place, in less than a day. Small moments make strong essays.
Write freely first. Then tap a sentence that feels general and press Zoom lens.
Answer any of the five questions in short notes. Then tap Drop notes under this sentence.
Dotted lines mark wide shots. Ask what moment shows each one.
Write what you thought then and what you think now. Then tap Pick a detail and tap the detail that changed it.
Tap Save version before big changes. Then try a new opening with Opening swap.
Tap a job chip for each paragraph. Then drag the cards to try a new order.
Version saved.
You're over your word limit. Look for a wide shot to cut.
Tap a highlighted detail to put your own words in The turn.
No close-up signals yet. Add a specific detail in Draft, or type the detail in The turn.
Pick an earlier and a later version to compare their words.
Type an alternate opening. Tap Try it to preview it, then Use this opening if it fits.
Read your essay aloud. Tick any private notes that fit.
Compare the two samples and their photographs. Tap Back to my writing to return.
Tap Add to the end of my draft, then edit the frame in Draft.
Your notes sit under the sentence. Rewrite them in Draft, then remove the note block.
Type a sentence in Draft, tap it, then press Zoom lens.
Clear your whole essay from this device?
This can't be undone. Clear?
Type a small moment in the box, then tap Add spark.
Tap Use this opening to replace only the first sentence. A version is saved first.
Write two paragraphs in Draft, then return to Sequence board.
Write what this detail changed in The turn. Then tap Draft an ending.
Choose the outcome, then tap Try this order to preview your sequence.
Choose Use this spark beside a saved moment to continue in Draft.
